chunks: I advise you, O servants of Allah, to have piety of Allah.

Who has furnished illustrations for you and timed for you your lives. He has given you covering of dress and scattered for you livelihood. He has surrounded you with His knowledge and ordained rewards. He has bestowed upon you vast bounties and extensive gifts. He has warned you through far-reaching arguments, and He has counted you by numbers. He has fixed for you ages in this place of test and house of instruction. You are on test in this world and have to render account about it.

key_terms.الْحِصَاءَ: Knowledge or counting (metaphorically surrounding with knowledge)

ai.seo_question: What are the key blessings of Allah mentioned in Nahj al-Balagha's Al-Gharra sermon?
ai.summary: This passage from the opening of *Al-Gharra* establishes the theological foundation of *taqwa* by linking divine providence—such as clothing, livelihood, and encompassing knowledge—to human accountability. In Shia exegesis, this enumeration serves as a rhetorical device to remind the audience that their testing in the 'abode of reflection' is a deliberate divine ordinance, reinforcing the concept that piety is the rational response to God's comprehensive care and clear proofs.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [Enjoining people to Piety] O creatures of Allāh I advise you to have fear of Allāh

Who has furnished illustrations and Who has timed for you your lives. He has given you covering of dress [1] and He has scattered for you livelihood. He has surrounded you with His knowledge. He has ordained rewards. He has bestowed upon you vast bounties and extensive gifts. He has warned you through far reaching arguments, and He has counted you by numbers. He has fixed for you ages (to live) in this place of test and house of instruction. You are on test in this world and have to render account about it.
